title: 6. 10-Year Financial Forensics, Cash Conversion & Balance Sheet
book_title: Follow the Cash: Ten-Year Forensics, Goodwill Bloat, and Balance Sheet Stress-Testing
question: Do Coforge's audited 10-year cash flows, return ratios, and post-Encora balance sheet support the profile of a durable compounder, or are debt, dilution, and intangibles masking fragility?

epigraph.quote: Profit is an accounting story; the balance sheet and cash flow statement are where M&A promises go to be audited.
epigraph.author: Financial Forensics Principle

web_blocks.html: From FY15 to FY26, Coforge built one of the cleanest growth records in Indian mid-tier IT [1, 6]. Sales grew 6.9x from ₹2,372 Cr to ₹16,403 Cr, a 18.4% 10-year median rate [1]. Operating profit climbed 8.7x from ₹337 Cr to ₹2,936 Cr, while Net Profit jumped 14.3x from ₹122 Cr to ₹1,745 Cr (29.4% 5-year CAGR) [1]. Then, in May 2026, the Encora deal reshaped the balance sheet [1, 6]. With two quarters of Encora included, TTM sales reached ₹20,380 Cr and TTM PAT hit ₹2,100 Cr [1].

web_blocks.caption: Coforge 12-Year Consolidated Profit & Loss Statement (FY15–TTM Sep 2026, ₹ Cr)
web_blocks.takeaway: Revenue compounded from ₹2,372 Cr (FY15) to ₹16,403 Cr (FY26) and ₹20,380 Cr TTM, with OPM expanding from 14% (FY15 and FY25) to 18% (FY26) and 19% TTM [1].

web_blocks.html: Cash conversion shows strong long-term health alongside recent strain [1]. From FY16 to FY25, cumulative Operating Cash Flow (CFO) hit ₹7,080 Cr against ₹5,468 Cr in PAT, a 129.5% ratio [1]. Free Cash Flow (FCF) totaled ₹4,598 Cr, or 84.1% of cumulative PAT [1]. In FY26, CFO of ₹1,792 Cr was 102.7% of PAT (₹1,745 Cr), and FCF of ₹1,197 Cr was 68.6% of PAT [1]. Screener's pre-tax CFO/EBITDA ratio also fell from 96% in FY25 to 76% in FY26 [1]. Two items explain that drop [1, 3]. First, a one-time Deferred Tax Liability reversal from the Cigniti merger cut FY26 tax to 13% versus the normal 21%–26% [1, 3]. Second, Debtor Days stretched from 78 to 88 days, tying up cash [1, 3].

web_blocks.caption: Coforge Consolidated Cash Flow & Cash Conversion History (FY15–FY26, ₹ Cr)
web_blocks.takeaway: CFO/EBITDA averaged ~96% across FY21–FY25 before moderating to 76% in FY26 as debtor days stretched to 88 and capex rose to ₹595 Cr [1].

web_blocks.html: The sharpest change sits on the September 2026 balance sheet [1, 13]. Before FY22, Coforge carried almost no debt, with borrowings of just ₹9–83 Cr [1]. Borrowings rose to ₹490 Cr in FY22 and ₹1,070 Cr in FY25 for SLK Global, then fell to ₹728 Cr by March 2026 [1, 10]. On May 1, 2026, Coforge closed the $2.35 billion Encora buyout [6]. It issued ~93.8 million new shares to Advent International and Warburg Pincus, diluting equity by ~20%–21.8% [1, 6, 7]. Equity Capital rose from ₹67 Cr to ₹89 Cr, and Reserves jumped from ₹9,470 Cr to ₹22,273 Cr [1, 6, 7]. Coforge also drew a $550 million 3-year term loan at 4.60%, lifting Borrowings from ₹728 Cr to ₹6,026 Cr [1, 6, 7]. Meanwhile, Fixed Assets—mostly goodwill and intangibles—surged from ₹6,760 Cr in March 2026 to ₹23,592 Cr in September 2026, or 68% of Total Assets (₹34,780 Cr) [1, 13].

web_blocks.caption: Coforge Consolidated Balance Sheet Transformation (FY15–Sep 2026, ₹ Cr)
web_blocks.takeaway: Encora transformed Coforge from a light-asset ₹728 Cr debt balance sheet (Mar 2026) into a ₹34,780 Cr balance sheet carrying ₹6,026 Cr debt and ₹23,592 Cr in fixed/intangible assets (Sep 2026) [1, 6, 13].

web_blocks.caption: Coforge Working Capital & Return Ratios (FY15–FY26)
web_blocks.takeaway: ROCE held in a strong 20%–32% band across the decade (24% in FY26, 23.5% latest), though post-Encora goodwill will mathematically compress reported ROCE until earnings scale [1].

web_blocks.takeaway: Coforge's 10-year cash generation, 23.5% ROCE, and CRISIL AA+/Stable rating earn a fundamental pass, but post-Encora leverage (₹6,026 Cr debt), intangible bloat (67.8% of assets), 110-day Total DSO, and a 21.8% PE sponsor block demand strict balance-sheet and governance discipline.

web_blocks.title: Screener Forensic Flags & Negative Other Income Explained
paragraphs: Automated screens flag a 13% FY26 tax rate, possible capitalized interest, and negative Other Income (-₹218 Cr TTM) [1]. The FY26 tax dip came from a one-time, non-cash Deferred Tax Liability reversal in the Cigniti merger, and tax normalized to 24% in both Q1 and Q2 FY27 [1, 3]. Interest expense rose from ₹40 Cr in Q4 FY26 to ₹87 Cr in Q1 FY27 and ₹108 Cr in Q2 FY27, confirming transparent P&L expensing of the $550M Encora loan [1, 7]. Finally, negative Other Income reflects legacy FX forward hedge losses ($10.2M in Q2 FY27), which management guides to drop to $7.1–7.5M in Q3 FY27, $1.2M in Q4 FY27, and zero thereafter.

book_paragraphs: Now you and I arrive at the moment of truth in any fundamental audit: stripping away the narrative and putting ten years of audited numbers under a forensic lamp. Does Coforge's cash flow match its earnings, and what did the Encora buyout do to its balance sheet?

First, look at the eleven-year compounding engine from FY15 to FY26. Consolidated revenue climbed nearly sevenfold from ₹2,372 Cr to ₹16,403 Cr—and ₹20,380 Cr on a trailing twelve-month basis through September 2026. Operating profit jumped from ₹337 Cr to ₹2,936 Cr, while net profit grew more than fourteenfold from ₹122 Cr to ₹1,745 Cr (a 29.4% five-year profit CAGR). Across the decade from FY16 to FY25, Coforge converted 129.5% of cumulative net profit into operating cash flow (₹7,080 Cr vs. ₹5,468 Cr) and 84.1% into free cash flow (₹4,598 Cr), all while earning 20% to 32% return on capital employed.

book_subsections.title: Cash Conversion Cracks and the FY26 Tax Optical Illusion
paragraphs: In FY26, however, two forensic cracks appeared that we must examine honestly. Operating cash flow was ₹1,792 Cr against ₹1,745 Cr of net profit (102.7%), and free cash flow was ₹1,197 Cr—meaning FCF conversion dropped to 68.6% of PAT, while Screener's CFO-to-EBITDA ratio fell from 96% in FY25 to 76% in FY26.

Part of that divergence was optical: FY26 net profit was boosted by a one-time, non-cash Deferred Tax Liability reversal from the Cigniti merger that temporarily dropped the effective tax rate to 13% before it normalized back to 24% in both Q1 and Q2 FY27. The more tangible drag was working capital, as debtor days stretched from 78 to 88 and capex stepped up to ₹595 Cr for global delivery and AI infrastructure.

book_subsections.title: The September 2026 Balance Sheet: Debt, Dilution, FX Hedges, and ₹23,592 Cr of Intangibles
paragraphs: Now look at the September 2026 balance sheet after Encora closed on May 1, 2026. Before Encora, Coforge was a light-asset business with ₹728 Cr of debt. Overnight, issuing roughly 93.8 million shares to Advent International and Warburg Pincus expanded equity capital from ₹67 Cr to ₹89 Cr and reserves from ₹9,470 Cr to ₹22,273 Cr—a ~21.8% equity dilution (bringing total shares to 44.31 Cr after the November 21, 2026 ESOP allotment). Simultaneously, drawing a $550 million three-year term loan at 4.60% pushed borrowings from ₹728 Cr to ₹6,026 Cr, while fixed and intangible assets—chiefly goodwill and acquired customer intangibles—ballooned from ₹6,760 Cr to ₹23,592 Cr, representing 67.8% of total assets (₹34,780 Cr).

Is that debt fatal? Not at Q2 FY27's run-rate: quarterly operating profit of ₹1,223 Cr covers quarterly interest of ₹108 Cr more than eleven times over, and CRISIL reaffirmed its AA+/Stable long-term rating on ₹6,148.2 Cr of bank facilities in July 2026, projecting net debt-to-EBITDA to remain at or below 2.0x in FY27. H1 FY27 free cash flow also improved to 92% of PAT ($53.8 million in Q2), and legacy FX hedge losses ($10.2 million in Q2 FY27, which drove negative Other Income) are guided to taper to $7.1–7.5 million in Q3, $1.2 million in Q4, and zero in FY28. Still, Q2 FY27 Total DSO stretched to 110 days (₹2,600 Cr net unbilled) during Encora entity novation, so over the next eight quarters you and I want to see Total DSO unwind, reported ROCE recover, and free cash flow steadily retire that ₹6,026 Cr debt pile.

callouts.title: The Tangible Asset Test Post-M&A
callouts.text: When 67.8% of a company's ₹34,780 Cr balance sheet sits in fixed and intangible assets (₹23,592 Cr), return on capital employed will mathematically compress until acquired earnings compound. Cash conversion, unbilled DSO normalization, and debt paydown—not accounting EPS—become the ultimate truth-tellers.

book_subsections.title: Post-Encora Balance Sheet Forensics: Debt, Goodwill & Dilution
paragraphs: A ten-year financial audit of Coforge splits cleanly into two chapters: the pre-Encora compounding decade (FY15–FY26) and the post-Encora balance sheet reset (May 2026 onward). Through March 2026, Coforge's balance sheet was pristine—borrowings stood at just ₹728 Cr against ₹16,403 Cr of revenue, ROCE was 23.5%, and ROE stood at 21.4%. The company funded organic growth and tuck-in deals like SLK Global and Cigniti largely out of internal accruals.

Closing the $2.35 billion Encora acquisition on May 1, 2026 changed the capital structure overnight. By September 2026, consolidated borrowings rose to ₹6,026 Cr (including the $550M syndicated term loan facility), fixed and intangible assets—predominantly goodwill and customer-relationship intangibles—expanded from ₹6,760 Cr to ₹23,592 Cr, and the share count expanded by roughly 20%. That is why headline ROE temporarily compressed to 13.46%. Going forward, earnings quality depends on two forensic checks: ensuring zero goodwill impairment surprises and watching net debt decline steadily out of ₹1,500–₹2,000 Cr+ of annual free cash flow.

book_subsections.title: Ten-Year Compounding Quality: Separating Organic Cash from M&A Optics
paragraphs: Zooming out across the full ten-year arc from FY15 to FY26, Coforge's financial record shows genuine operating leverage rather than financial engineering. Sales compounded more than sixfold from ₹2,372 Cr to ₹16,403 Cr, operating profit expanded from ₹346 Cr to ₹2,936 Cr, and operating margins climbed from 15% to 18% even as the company invested heavily in US/European sales leadership.

Before Encora closed in May 2026, Coforge consistently generated 20%+ ROCE and 20%+ ROE with minimal net debt. Now that Encora's $2.35B enterprise value sits on the balance sheet, the next eight quarters will test whether the combined entity can restore ROCE back toward 20% and pay down its ₹6,026 Cr debt load out of internal free cash flow.

For institutional investors, the cleanest way to track that deleveraging is to watch quarterly net debt-to-EBITDA and interest coverage alongside unbilled revenue days. In FY26, Coforge generated ₹1,792 Cr of operating cash flow and ₹1,197 Cr of free cash flow on ₹16,403 Cr of revenue. With the combined Coforge-Encora platform now annualizing nearly ₹24,700 Cr in revenue and targeting 16.0% to 17.0% EBIT margins, normalized annual free cash flow should expand meaningfully above ₹2,000 Cr once one-time integration and legal-entity restructuring costs roll off. That cash-generation capacity is what gives Coforge a realistic path to retire its syndicated term loan ahead of schedule while preserving shareholder returns.

book_callouts.title: Why Dividend Payouts May Stay Modest Near Term
book_callouts.text: Historically, Coforge maintained a healthy ~36% dividend payout ratio (34% in FY26). With ₹6,026 Cr of post-Encora debt on the balance sheet, retaining cash for debt reduction should take priority over aggressive dividend hikes.
